exercises.name: 90/90 Hamstring
exercises.description: Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out. With the other leg, bend the hip and knee to 90 degrees. You may brace your leg with your hands if necessary. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.description: Kneel holding an ab wheel. Roll forward until your torso is extended, bracing your core to prevent your back from sagging. Pull back to the start using your abs. One of the hardest ab exercises.

exercises.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
exercises.description: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand. Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: Start with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you. As you press up, rotate your palms forward so they face away at the top. Reverse on the way down. Hits all three deltoid heads.

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.description: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench. Lower your upper body toward the floor, then raise it back to parallel or slightly above. Targets the spinal erectors and can also work the glutes.

exercises.name: Back Squat (BB)
exercises.description: Bar sits on your upper traps. Brace core, push knees out and squat until thighs are at least parallel to the floor. Drive through the whole foot to stand. The king of lower-body exercises.

exercises.name: Banded Clamshell
exercises.description: Lie on your side with knees bent and a band above the knees. Keeping feet together, rotate the top knee upward like a clamshell opening. Targets the gluteus medius and external hip rotators.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Sit with your upper back against a bench, bar over your hips. Drive through your heels to thrust your hips upward until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Squeeze glutes hard at the top, then lower.

exercises.name: Bench Dips
exercises.description:
• Sit on the edge of a bench, hands gripping the edge, fingers forward
• Extend your legs out in front, heels on the floor
• Slide your hips off the bench so your arms support your weight
• Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor
• Press back up through your palms to full arm extension

exercises.name: Bench Press (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Lie on a flat bench, gripping a barbell just outside shoulder width or holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level. Lower the weight to your mid-chest with elbows at roughly 45°, then press back up to lockout. The foundational horizontal push.

exercises.name: Bent Over Low-Pulley Side Lateral
exercises.description:
• Stand bent at the waist, torso near parallel to the floor, side-on to a low pulley
• Hold the handle with your far hand, arm hanging down
• Raise your arm out to the side until in line with your shoulder, leading with the elbow
• Keep a slight bend in the arm throughout
• Lower with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Bent-Arm Pullover (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Lie perpendicular across a flat bench with only your shoulders supported, holding a dumbbell or barbell straight over your chest with a slight bend in your arms. Lower the weight behind your head in an arc, feeling a stretch through the lats and chest, then pull back over your chest.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
exercises.description: Lay flat on the floor with your arms next to your sides. Now bend your knees at around a 75 degree angle and lift your feet off the floor by around 2 inches.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Row (DB/BB/KB)
exercises.description: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, holding a barbell, a dumbbell in each hand, or a pair of kettlebells. Row the weight to your lower chest or navel, driving your elbows back and retracting your shoulder blades. Lower under control.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: Lie on your back, legs raised, hands behind head. Bring opposite elbow to knee while extending the other leg. Alternate sides in a pedalling motion to target both the rectus abdominis and obliques.

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.description:
• Set up in a power rack with a box behind you at your target depth
• Rack a barbell on your upper back as in a back squat
• Descend under control until you sit lightly on the box
• Pause briefly without relaxing your brace
• Drive back up through your heels to standing

exercises.name: Bradford/Rocky Presses
exercises.description:
• Sit on a bench with back support, bar racked at shoulder height, pronated grip
• Press the bar up until your arms are extended
• Lower the bar behind your head to touch your upper traps
• Press back up and lower to the front, without fully locking out between reps
• Alternate front-to-back presses for the set

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (DB)
exercises.description: Elevate your rear foot on a bench, front foot forward, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your front shin as vertical as possible. Drive through the front heel to stand.

exercises.name: Butterfly
exercises.description: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad. Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press
exercises.description:
• Set both pulleys to chest height, sit or stand between the towers
• Grip a handle in each hand, elbows bent ~90°, upper arms at about 45° from your torso
• Press the handles forward until your arms are extended
• Squeeze your chest at full extension
• Return with control

exercises.name: Cable Crossover
exercises.description: Set cables at shoulder height on both sides. Step forward and bring the handles together in front of your chest in a hugging motion, crossing slightly at the bottom to maximise pec contraction.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.description: Kneel facing a high cable pulley, rope attached. Hold the rope behind your head and crunch your elbows toward your knees, rounding the spine. The cable provides constant tension through the full range.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
exercises.description: Stand facing a low cable pulley, grip the handle underhand. Curl from full extension to full contraction, keeping tension on the bicep throughout the movement via the cable.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.description: Set a cable at face height with a rope attachment. Pull the rope toward your face splitting the hands at the end, with elbows high and wide. Excellent for rear delt health and external rotation strength.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.description: Stand in front of a low pulley facing forward with one leg next to the pulley and the other one away. Attach the ankle cuff to the cable and also to the ankle of the leg that is next to the pulley.

exercises.name: Cable Kickback
exercises.description: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable. Brace on the machine and kick the attached leg straight back and up in a hip extension movement, squeezing the glute at the top. Avoid rotating your hips.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Set a low cable to one side. Raise the handle out away from the cable until your arm is at shoulder height. The cable maintains constant tension throughout — particularly effective at the bottom range.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Adjust the pulleys to the appropriate height and adjust the weight. The pulleys should be above your head. Grab the left pulley with your right hand and the right pulley with your left hand, crossing them in front of you. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
• Attach a rope to a low pulley
• Face away from the machine, rope held overhead in both hands, neutral grip, elbows close to your head
• Extend your arms until straight, splitting the rope ends apart slightly at the top
• Bend your elbows to lower back down behind your head
• Keep elbows fixed throughout

exercises.name: Cable Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight. Stand directly in between the uprights. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Shrugs
exercises.description: Grasp a cable bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a shoulder width or slightly wider overhand (palms facing down) grip. Stand erect close to the pulley with your arms extended in front of you holding the bar. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.description: Support on parallel bars but lean your torso forward. Lower until upper arms are parallel to the floor, then press back up. The forward lean shifts the load to the lower chest rather than the triceps.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Incline Row (DB)
exercises.description: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench. Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width. Pull until your chin clears the bar. The underhand grip recruits the biceps more heavily than a standard pull-up.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.description: Set up like a bench press but with hands shoulder-width or narrower. Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows tucked close to your sides. Press back up, focusing on the triceps.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
exercises.description:
• Sit at a lat pulldown station, thighs secured under the pads
• Grip the bar with hands closer than shoulder width, palms facing away
• Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and back
• Squeeze your lats at the bottom
• Let the bar rise with control back to full arm extension

exercises.name: Close-Grip Upright Row (BB)
exercises.description: Hold a barbell or cable with a narrow overhand grip. Pull the weight straight up to chin height, leading with your elbows. The narrow grip shifts emphasis to the side delts vs a wide grip.

exercises.name: Cocoons
exercises.description:
• Lie on your back, legs straight, arms extended behind your head
• Simultaneously curl your knees toward your chest and your arms/torso forward
• Rotate your pelvis to lift your hips off the floor at the top
• Pause briefly in the tucked position
• Uncurl with control back to the start

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.description: Sit on a bench, brace your elbow on the inside of your thigh. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, fully contracting the bicep. Excellent isolation — no body swing allowed.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent. Place hands behind your head and curl your upper spine off the floor, contracting the rectus abdominis. Lower with control. Avoid pulling on your neck.

exercises.name: Cuban Press
exercises.description:
• Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging, pronated grip
• Raise your upper arms out to the sides to parallel with the floor (scarecrow position), forearms hanging down
• Externally rotate your shoulders to bring the dumbbells up so forearms point overhead
• Press the dumbbells straight overhead
• Reverse the sequence to return to the start

exercises.name: Curl (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Stand holding a barbell or a pair of dumbbells at hip height with an underhand grip. Curl the weight up toward your chest, keeping elbows pinned at your sides. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on your back with arms raised toward the ceiling and knees at 90°. Extend one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor while maintaining a flat lower back. Return and switch sides.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.description: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, grip just outside your legs. Hinge down, brace your core, then drive the floor away to stand. The ultimate full-body pull — lats and traps keep the bar close.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Set the bench to a 15–30° decline. Lower a barbell or a dumbbell in each hand to your lower chest, then press back up. The decline angle preferentially loads the sternal head of the pec.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.description: Place your hands together under your chest forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers. Lower your chest toward your hands, then push back up. Heavily taxes the medial head.

exercises.name: Dip Machine
exercises.description: Sit securely in a dip machine, select the weight and firmly grasp the handles. Now keep your elbows in at your sides in order to place emphasis on the triceps. The elbows should be bent at a 90 degree angle.

exercises.name: Double Leg Butt Kick
exercises.description: Begin standing with your knees slightly bent. Quickly squat a short distance, flexing the hips and knees, and immediately extend to jump for maximum vertical height.

exercises.name: Drag Curl
exercises.description:
• Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, elbows pulled back and close to your torso
• Curl the bar upward while keeping it dragging in contact with your body
• Keep your elbows traveling backward rather than forward as the bar rises
• Squeeze at the top
• Lower with control, staying in contact with your torso

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
exercises.description: Lie on a bench and grip it above your head. Lift your entire body off the bench, supported only at your shoulders. Lower your body in a straight rigid line, then raise back up. Extremely demanding.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
exercises.description:
• Lie face down on an incline bench, chest supported
• Let a dumbbell hang in each hand, arms fully extended
• Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders
• Squeeze your biceps at the top
• Lower with control back to full extension

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Flye
exercises.description: Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Raise both arms out to the sides in a flye motion, leading with your elbows. Squeeze the rear delts at the top.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Scaption
exercises.description:
• Stand holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, thumbs pointing up
• Raise your arms out in front of you at about 30° from your body (between a front raise and lateral raise)
• Lift to shoulder height
• Pause briefly
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench. Sit on a flat bench and place a dumbbell on your upper left thigh about 3 inches above your knee.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squat
exercises.description:
• Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides
• Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out
• Bend your knees and hips to squat down, keeping your chest up
• Descend until thighs are at least parallel to the floor
• Drive through your feet to stand back up

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.description:
• Hold an EZ-curl bar at the angled outer grips, palms facing forward
• Keep your elbows pinned at your sides
• Curl the bar up toward your chest
• Squeeze your biceps at the top
• Lower with control back to full extension

exercises.name: Elbow to Knee
exercises.description:
• Lie on your back, hands clasped behind your head
• Cross one leg over, resting that ankle on the opposite bent knee
• Curl your torso, rotating to bring the opposite elbow toward the raised knee
• Pause briefly at the contraction
• Lower with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Elevated Cable Rows
exercises.description: Get a platform of some sort (it can be an aerobics or calf raise platform) that is around 4-6 inches in height. Place it on the seat of the cable row machine.

exercises.name: Elevated Reverse Lunge (BB)
exercises.description: Position a bar onto a rack at shoulder height loaded to an appropriate weight. Place a short, raised platform behind you. Rack the bar onto your upper back, keeping your back arched and tight. Step onto your raised platform with both feet. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: External Rotation
exercises.description: Lie on your side holding a light dumbbell, or use a cable at waist height. With the elbow fixed at 90°, rotate the forearm up and outward. Targets the infraspinatus and teres minor — key rotator cuff health work.

exercises.name: External Rotation with Cable
exercises.description:
• Set a cable at elbow height, stand side-on to the machine
• Grip the handle with your far hand, elbow bent 90° and pinned to your side
• Keeping the elbow fixed, rotate your forearm outward away from your body
• Pause at full rotation
• Return with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Finger Curls
exercises.description: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing up; hands spaced about shoulder width. Place your feet flat on the floor, at a distance that is slightly wider than shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Flat Bench Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: Lie with your back flat on a bench and your legs extended in front of you off the end. Place your hands either under your glutes with your palms down or by the sides holding on to the bench. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Flye
exercises.description: Lie flat on a bench holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing in. Lower your arms out in a wide arc until you feel a deep pec stretch, then squeeze back to the top.

exercises.name: Floor Press
exercises.description:
• Lie on the floor with a barbell racked at an appropriate height above you
• Grip the bar at shoulder width and pull it off the rack
• Lower the bar until your upper arms touch the floor
• Pause briefly
• Press back up to full extension

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description:
• Lie face down on a bench, hips at the edge, holding the front edge with your hands
• Extend your legs straight out behind you, toes pointed
• Squeeze your glutes and raise your legs until level with your hips
• Alternate small up-and-down flutter kicks with straight legs
• Keep your core braced throughout

exercises.name: Front Cable Raise
exercises.description:
• Stand facing away from a low pulley, handle in one hand in front of your thighs
• Keep a slight bend in your elbow
• Raise your arm straight up in front of you to shoulder height
• Pause briefly
• Lower with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Front Dumbbell Raise
exercises.description:
• Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs
• Keep your torso still, no swinging
• Raise one arm straight up in front of you to shoulder height
• Lower with control
• Alternate arms each rep

exercises.name: Front Incline Dumbbell Raise
exercises.description:
• Sit on an incline bench set to 30–60°, holding a dumbbell in each hand
• Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing down
• Raise your arms straight in front of you to shoulder height
• Pause briefly at the top
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Front Leg Raises
exercises.description: Stand next to a chair or other support, holding on with one hand. Swing your leg forward, keeping the leg straight. Continue with a downward swing, bringing the leg as far back as your flexibility allows. Repeat 5-10 times, and then switch legs.

exercises.name: Front Raise (DB)
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and raise both arms straight in front of you to shoulder height. Lower with control. Isolates the anterior deltoid. Can also be done with a plate or cable.

exercises.name: Front Squat (BB)
exercises.description: Bar rests on your front delts with elbows high. Squat down keeping your torso upright — this makes it harder than a back squat but places more emphasis on the quads and demands more core stability.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Glute Ham Raise
exercises.description:
• Set up on a glute-ham developer, feet secured against the footplate, knees just behind the pad
• Start face down with your back arched
• Curl your body upward by flexing your knees and driving your hips forward
• Rise until your body is upright
• Lower with control back to the start

exercises.name: Glute Kickback
exercises.description:
• Get on your hands and knees, arms extended, shoulder-width apart
• Keep your core braced and back flat
• Kick one leg straight back and up, squeezing the glute at the top
• Avoid rotating your hips or arching your lower back
• Lower with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands. Squat deep, pushing knees out over your toes. The front-loaded weight helps keep your torso upright — excellent for learning squat mechanics.

exercises.name: Good Morning (BB)
exercises.description:
• Rack a barbell across your upper back, as in a squat
• Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent and fixed
• Hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back flat, until your torso is near parallel to the floor
• Feel the stretch through your hamstrings
• Drive your hips forward to return to standing

exercises.name: Groiners
exercises.description: Begin in a pushup position on the floor. This will be your starting position. Using both legs, jump forward landing with your feet next to your hands. Keep your head up as you do so.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.description: Position yourself on the machine with feet on the platform and back against the pad. Lower until thighs are parallel, then press back up. The fixed path with feet forward increases quad isolation.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Hold dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Curl the weight up while keeping the hammer grip throughout. Targets the brachialis and brachioradialis more than a standard curl.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms. Raise your legs (bent or straight) until they are parallel to the floor or higher. Lower with control, avoiding swinging.

exercises.name: Hanging Pike
exercises.description:
• Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width
• Keep your legs together and straight
• Bend your knees to 90° and bring them up
• Continue raising your hips and legs until your body forms a pike
• Lower with control back to a full hang

exercises.name: Hip Abductor Machine
exercises.description: Sit in the machine with the pads on the outside of your knees, upper body stationary. Push your legs outward against the resistance, squeezing at the end range. Targets the gluteus medius and hip abductors in isolation.

exercises.name: Hip Circles (prone)
exercises.description: Position yourself on your hands and knees on the ground. Maintaining good posture, raise one bent knee off of the ground. This will be your starting position. Keeping the knee in a bent position, rotate the femur in an arc, attempting to make a big circle with your knee.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench
exercises.description:
• Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the edge
• Have a partner hold your legs down
• Let your upper body hang toward the floor
• Raise your torso using your lower back until in line with your legs
• Lower with control back down

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.description:
• Stand with feet close together, legs straight
• Bend forward and place your hands on the floor
• Walk your hands forward into a plank position
• Walk your feet forward to meet your hands, keeping legs as straight as possible
• Repeat the sequence

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Set the bench to 30–45°. Lower a barbell to your upper chest, or press dumbbells up from shoulder level allowing a slight inward arc at the top. The incline shifts emphasis onto the upper pecs and anterior delts.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Chest Press
exercises.description:
• Set both pulleys to a lower position, sit on an incline bench between the towers
• Grip a handle in each hand, elbows bent ~90°
• Press the handles up and forward until your arms are extended
• Squeeze your upper chest at full extension
• Return with control

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Flye
exercises.description: Perform the flye on an incline bench to shift the stretch and contraction toward the upper chest. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and avoid letting the arms drop too low.

exercises.name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench. The dumbbells should be at arm\'s length hanging at your sides and your palms should be facing out. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up Medium
exercises.description: Stand facing a Smith machine bar or sturdy elevated platform at an appropriate height. Place your hands on the bar, with your hands about shoulder width apart.

exercises.name: JM Press
exercises.description:
• Lie on a flat bench, holding a barbell at arm's length with a close grip, elbows in
• Lower the bar toward your neck/chin in a path between a skull crusher and a close-grip bench press
• Keep elbows pointed forward, not flared
• Press back up to full extension
• Repeat with control

exercises.name: Jefferson Squat (BB)
exercises.description: Place a barbell on the floor. Stand in the middle of the bar length wise.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description:
• Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder and press it overhead with one arm, locked out
• Turn your feet roughly 45° away from that arm
• Keeping the kettlebell overhead and eyes on it, hinge sideways at the hips toward your front foot
• Slide your free hand down your leg toward the floor
• Reverse the movement to return to standing

exercises.name: Knee Circles
exercises.description: Stand with your legs together and hands by your waist. Now move your knees in a circular motion as you breathe normally.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Place a bench sideways in front of a high pulley machine. Hold a straight bar attachment above your head with your hands about 6 inches apart with your palms facing down.

exercises.name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
exercises.description:
• Set a pulley above head height, attach a rope
• Kneel a couple of feet away, arms extended holding the rope
• Pull the rope down and back by flexing your elbows, driving them toward your hips
• Squeeze your back at the bottom
• Extend your arms back out with control

exercises.name: Landmine Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Stand sideways to a loaded landmine, grip the collar end. Raise the bar out to the side in an arcing motion to shoulder height. The angled resistance makes this a joint-friendly lateral raise variation.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.description: Press a barbell (loaded on one end in a landmine or corner) from shoulder height up and forward in an arcing path. The angle mimics an incline press while being easier on the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Leg Curl
exercises.description: Lie face-down in the machine or sit in a seated version. Curl your legs against the pad toward your glutes, squeezing the hamstrings at full contraction. Lower slowly back to start.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: Sit in the machine with the pad on your lower shins. Extend your legs fully against the resistance, squeezing the quads at the top. Lower with control. A direct quad isolation exercise.

exercises.name: Leg Lift
exercises.description:
• Stand tall, holding a stable support for balance
• Keep your standing leg slightly bent
• Lift the other leg straight back behind you, squeezing the glute
• Keep your torso upright, avoid leaning forward
• Lower with control, then switch legs

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: Sit in the machine with feet at shoulder width on the platform. Lower the sled until your knees are at 90°, then press back to near-lockout. Foot placement can shift emphasis to quads vs hamstrings.

exercises.name: Leverage Chest Press
exercises.description: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height. The handles should be near the bottom or middle of the pectorals at the beginning of the motion. Your chest and head should be up and your shoulder blades retracted. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Leverage Decline Chest Press
exercises.description:
• Sit in the machine with the seat adjusted so handles start at the bottom of your chest
• Keep your chest up and shoulder blades retracted
• Press the handles forward and up until your arms are extended
• Squeeze your lower chest
• Return with control

exercises.name: Leverage High Row
exercises.description:
• Adjust the seat so you can reach the handles above you, knee pad locked in
• Grip the handles with a pronated grip
• Pull the handles down toward your torso, driving elbows back
• Squeeze your back at the bottom
• Extend your arms back up with control

exercises.name: Leverage Incline Chest Press
exercises.description:
• Sit in the machine with handles starting near the top of your chest
• Keep your chest up and shoulder blades retracted
• Press the handles forward and up until your arms are extended
• Squeeze your upper chest
• Return with control

exercises.name: Leverage Shoulder Press
exercises.description:
• Sit in the machine, seat adjusted so handles start near your shoulders
• Grip the handles with a pronated grip, chest and head up
• Press the handles straight overhead until your arms are extended
• Pause briefly
• Lower with control back to the start

exercises.name: Lower Back Curl
exercises.description:
• Lie face down, arms out to your sides
• Keep your legs and hips on the floor
• Using only your lower back muscles, lift your chest off the floor
• Don't push with your arms
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Lunge (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Holding a barbell on your back or a dumbbell in each hand, step forward into a lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor. Keep your torso upright, then push back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Lying Crossover
exercises.description:
• Lie on your back, legs extended, a partner kneeling beside you
• Cross one leg over your body, bent knee reaching toward the floor on the opposite side
• Partner holds your opposite shoulder down and controls the crossed leg for a stretch
• Hold briefly
• Return and switch sides

exercises.name: Lying Glute
exercises.description:
• Lie on your back, partner kneeling beside you
• Raise one leg, rotating it so the foot crosses over the opposite hip, lower leg perpendicular to your body
• Partner holds your knee and ankle to apply a stretch
• Hold briefly
• Return and switch sides

exercises.name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
exercises.description:
• Lie face down, partner kneeling beside you
• Bend one knee, raising that foot toward your glutes
• Partner holds your knee and ankle, gently deepening the stretch
• Hold briefly
• Return and switch legs

exercises.name: Lying Rear Delt Raise (DB)
exercises.description: Lie face-down on a flat or slightly inclined bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip and arms extended, elbows slightly bent. Raise your arms out to the sides until in line with your shoulders, squeezing the rear delts, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Machine Bicep Curl
exercises.description: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position. Perform the movement by flexing the elbow, pulling your lower arm towards your upper arm.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder (Military) Press
exercises.description: Sit down on the Shoulder Press Machine and select the weight. Grab the handles to your sides as you keep the elbows bent and in line with your torso. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Machine Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position. Perform the movement by extending the elbow, pulling your lower arm away from your upper arm.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl
exercises.description: Anchor your feet and start kneeling upright. Lower your torso slowly toward the floor, resisting with your hamstrings — ideally going all the way down. Use hands to push up if needed. Extremely effective for hamstring strength and injury prevention.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat
exercises.description:
• Grip a barbell wider than shoulder width, pronated grip
• Press the bar overhead, arms locked out, bar balanced over your midfoot
• Keeping the bar overhead throughout, squat down with feet wider than shoulder width
• Descend until thighs are at least parallel to the floor
• Drive up through your heels back to standing, bar staying overhead

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (DB)
exercises.description: Stand holding a dumbbell with both hands overhead, arms fully extended. Lower the weight behind your head by bending at the elbows, then extend back up. Maximally stretches the long head of the tricep. Can also be done with a cable.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.description: Stand sideways to a cable machine, holding the handle at chest height. Press the handle straight out, resisting the rotational pull of the cable. A true anti-rotation core exercise.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.description: Sit at the machine with arms on the pads at chest height. Bring the pads together in front of your chest, squeezing the pecs hard at the peak. Lower slowly to maintain tension.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: Hold a straight-body position on forearms and toes, forming a rigid plank from head to heel. Brace your core and glutes. Hold for time, focusing on not letting your hips sag or pike.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Rest your upper arms on the preacher pad with an underhand grip. Curl the bar or dumbbells up from full extension, focusing on the peak contraction. Lower slowly to avoid hyperextension.

exercises.name: Preacher Hammer Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Place the upper part of both arms on top of the preacher bench as you hold a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip). As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.

exercises.name: Pull Through
exercises.description:
• Straddle a low pulley, cable running between your legs, rope or handle attached
• Face away from the machine, feet wide
• Hinge at the hips, reaching through your legs as far as comfortable, soft knees
• Drive your hips forward to stand, squeezing your glutes at the top
• Repeat with control

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder width. Pull until your chin clears the bar, squeezing your lats. Lower back to a full hang. One of the best compound back builders.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: Start in a high plank with hands just outside shoulder width. Lower your chest to the floor with elbows at 45°, then press back up to full arm extension. A foundational bodyweight chest exercise.

exercises.name: Push-Ups With Feet Elevated
exercises.description:
• Get into a push-up position with your toes on top of a bench or box
• Hands slightly wider than shoulder width
• Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45°
• Press back up to full extension
• Keep your body in a straight line throughout

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.description: Set bar pins at knee height. Pull the bar from this elevated position to full lockout, focusing on the upper back and traps. Allows heavier loading than a full deadlift.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.description: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip. Curl the bar up keeping the overhand position throughout. Heavily targets the brachioradialis and forearm extensors.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Bent-Over Rows
exercises.description:
• Hold a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip
• Hinge forward at the hips, knees slightly bent, back flat, torso near parallel to floor
• Row the bar to your lower ribcage, elbows staying close to your body
• Squeeze your back at the top
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description:
• Set a bar attachment on a high pulley
• Grip it with palms facing up, shoulder width
• Keeping elbows pinned at your sides, push the bar down until your arms are extended
• Squeeze your triceps at the bottom
• Let the bar rise back up with control

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.description: Lie face-down on a bench with hips at the edge and legs hanging. Raise your legs behind you using your glutes and hamstrings until they are parallel to the floor. Lower with control.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (DB)
exercises.description: Holding a dumbbell in each hand, step backward into a lunge, lowering the rear knee to the floor. Push through the front foot to return to standing. The reverse direction is more knee-friendly than a forward lunge.

exercises.name: Reverse Machine Flyes
exercises.description:
• Sit facing into the machine, handles set to the rear, seat adjusted so handles are at shoulder height
• Grip the handles with palms facing inward
• Pull your arms back and apart in a semicircular motion, squeezing your rear delts and upper back
• Pause at full contraction
• Return with control

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.description: Sit facing into the machine with arms extended forward. Drive both arms back and apart in a reverse hugging motion, squeezing the rear delts and rhomboids at the end range. Lower with control.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: Hold a barbell at hip height, soft bend in knees. Hinge at the hips, pushing them back and lowering the bar along your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch. Drive hips forward to stand.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.description: Sit on the floor with knees bent, torso leaned back slightly. Rotate the weight (or your hands) from side to side, twisting through the waist. Add a pause at each side for greater oblique engagement.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Military Press
exercises.description:
• Sit on a bench with back support, bar behind your head at the base of your neck (spotter hands it to you)
• Grip the bar wider than shoulder width, pronated grip
• Press the bar straight overhead until your arms are extended
• Lower slowly back down behind your head
• Repeat with control

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Twist
exercises.description:
• Sit at the end of a flat bench, feet flat and shoulder-width apart
• Rest a barbell across your thighs, gripping it wider than shoulder width
• Rotate your torso to one side as far as comfortable, then back through center to the other side
• Keep your hips facing forward throughout
• Movement stays in the torso, not the hips

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
exercises.description: Place a couple of dumbbells looking forward in front of a flat bench. Sit on the end of the bench with your legs together and the dumbbells behind your calves.

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description:
• Sit at the end of a bench, knees bent, torso bent forward until near parallel to floor
• Hold a dumbbell in each hand behind you, neutral grip, elbows bent
• Extend your arms straight back, keeping upper arms still
• Squeeze your triceps at full extension
• Bend elbows to lower back with control

exercises.name: Seated Biceps
exercises.description:
• Sit on the floor, knees bent, partner standing behind you
• Extend your arms straight behind you, palms facing each other, partner holding your wrists
• Attempt to flex your elbows, curling your hands toward you against the partner's resistance
• Hold briefly at peak contraction
• Return to extension and repeat

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: Sit in the machine with the pad on your lower thighs. Raise your heels as high as possible by pushing through the balls of your feet. The seated position isolates the soleus more than the standing version.

exercises.name: Seated Front Deltoid
exercises.description:
• Sit upright on the floor, legs bent, partner standing behind you
• Extend your arms straight out to your sides, palms facing down, partner holding your wrists
• Attempt to move your arms as far behind you as possible against the partner's resistance
• Hold briefly
• Return to the start and repeat

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Press (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a barbell or a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Press the weight overhead until your arms are fully extended, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Press
exercises.description:
• Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell overhead with both hands
• Keep your upper arms close to your head, elbows pointed forward
• Lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows
• Pause at full stretch
• Extend back up to full arm extension

exercises.name: Shrug (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs or a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Elevate your shoulders as high as possible, hold the contraction for a second, then lower with control. Keep your arms fully extended throughout.

exercises.name: Side Bend (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Stand up straight holding a dumbbell in one hand, or a barbell across the back of your shoulders. Keeping your back straight and head up, bend at the waist to one side as far as comfortable, then return to standing. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Side Jackknife
exercises.description: Perform Side Jackknife with controlled form.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: Lie on your side and lift your hips off the ground, supporting yourself on one forearm and the edge of one foot. Maintain a straight line from head to feet. Targets the obliques and quadratus lumborum.

exercises.name: Side Split Squat (BB)
exercises.description:
• Rack a barbell across your upper back
• Stand with feet very wide, toes of the working leg turned slightly out
• Shift your weight to that side and bend that knee deeply, keeping the other leg straight
• Lower until your hamstring nears your calf
• Drive back up through the bent leg, then repeat on the other side

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Plant one knee and hand on a bench for support. Row the dumbbell toward your hip keeping your torso parallel to the floor. Focus on driving the elbow back rather than just lifting the weight.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift (KB)
exercises.description: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand. Stand on one leg, on the same side that you hold the kettlebell. Keeping that knee slightly bent, perform a stiff legged deadlift by bending at the hip, extending your free leg behind you for balance.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Lie on a bench holding a barbell, EZ-bar, or a dumbbell in each hand above your chest with elbows tucked in. Bend only at the elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead, then press back to extension. Keep upper arms vertical throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description:
• Set a flat bench under the Smith machine bar
• Lie down with the bar positioned over your chest at an appropriate height
• Grip the bar wider than shoulder width, pronated grip
• Unrack and lower the bar to your mid-chest
• Press back up to full extension

exercises.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
exercises.description: Place a block or weight plate below the bar on the Smith machine. Set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step onto the plates with the balls of your feet and place the bar on the back of your shoulders.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description:
• Set the bar to shoulder height, step under it, rest it across your upper back
• Unrack and step your feet forward slightly, shoulder-width apart
• Squat down until thighs are at least parallel to the floor
• Drive through your feet to stand back up
• Re-rack the bar at the end of the set

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.description:
• Set up on the front side of a preacher bench, chest and stomach against the pad, arms hanging down
• Hold a barbell or EZ-bar with an underhand grip
• Curl the bar up toward your chin
• Squeeze your biceps at the top
• Lower with control back to full extension

exercises.name: Standing Cable Lift
exercises.description:
• Set a pulley to its lowest position, attach a handle
• Stand side-on to the machine, arm's length away, grip the handle with your far hand
• Rotate and lift diagonally, pulling the handle up and across your body to above your opposite shoulder
• Pivot your back foot as you rotate
• Return with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
exercises.description:
• Set a pulley to its highest position, attach a handle
• Stand side-on to the machine, arm's length away, grip the handle with your far hand
• Rotate and pull diagonally downward across your body toward your opposite hip
• Pivot your back foot as you rotate
• Return with control, then switch sides

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (DB)
exercises.description: Stand with the balls of your feet on an elevated surface, holding a dumbbell in each hand for added resistance. Lower your heels as far as possible, then rise up onto your toes as high as you can go. Pause at the top and squeeze. Lower slowly.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Circles
exercises.description: Begin standing on one leg, holding to a vertical support. Raise the unsupported knee to 90 degrees. This will be your starting position.

exercises.name: Standing Overhead Press (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Standing with a barbell racked at shoulder height or a dumbbell in each hand, press the weight overhead until your arms are extended, allowing a slight inward arc at the top. Brace your core to avoid leaning back.

exercises.name: Step-Up (DB)
exercises.description: Stand in front of a box or bench holding a dumbbell in each hand. Step up with one foot, drive through that heel to bring your full body onto the box. Step back down and repeat. Keep your torso upright throughout.

exercises.name: Step-up with Knee Raise
exercises.description:
• Stand facing a box or bench, feet together
• Step up, placing one foot on top of the box
• Extend through the hip and knee to stand fully on the box
• Drive your opposite knee up toward your chest at the top
• Step back down with control, then switch legs

exercises.name: Stiff-Legged Deadlift (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Holding a barbell or a dumbbell in each hand with a straight torso and a shoulder-width or narrower stance, knees slightly bent, hinge at the hips and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch. Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

exercises.name: Stomach Vacuum
exercises.description:
• Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands on your hips
• Inhale fully
• Exhale completely, drawing your stomach in as far as possible
• Hold the contracted position, continuing to breathe shallowly
• Release and repeat

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.description:
• Place a dumbbell upright on one end of a flat bench
• Lie perpendicular across the bench, only your shoulders supported, hips below the bench
• Hold the dumbbell straight above your chest with both hands, arms locked
• Lower the dumbbell back over your head until you feel a stretch through your lats
• Pull back over your chest, keeping your arms straight throughout

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: Stand facing a high cable pulley, arms extended overhead. Keeping your arms straight, pull the bar down to your thighs using only shoulder extension. Isolates the lats without bicep involvement.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: Take a wide stance with toes pointed out and grip the bar inside your legs. Hinge down keeping your back flat and chest up, then drive the floor away to stand. The wide stance loads the glutes and adductors heavily.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Take a wide stance with toes turned out. Hold a barbell on your back or a single dumbbell/kettlebell at the base with both hands in front of you. Squat down keeping your knees tracking over your toes and chest tall. The wide stance increases glute and inner-thigh activation versus a standard squat.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description:
• Lie face down, arms fully extended in front of you
• Simultaneously raise your arms, chest, and legs off the floor
• Squeeze your lower back and glutes at the top
• Hold briefly
• Lower with control

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.description: Straddle the bar with a neutral grip on the handle. Keep your back flat and hinge forward, then row the weight to your lower chest. A thicker bar path hits the lats and teres major hard.

exercises.name: Tate Press
exercises.description:
• Lie on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other
• Keep elbows flared out to the sides, upper arms roughly perpendicular to your torso
• Lower the dumbbells by bending your elbows until they nearly touch your chest
• Keep elbows high and stationary throughout
• Press back up to full extension

exercises.name: Thigh Adductor
exercises.description:
• Sit in the adductor machine, legs positioned on the pads
• Grip the handles, upper body stationary
• Press your legs together against the resistance
• Squeeze your inner thighs at the end range
• Return with control to the start

exercises.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.description:
• Hold a dumbbell in each hand, knees slightly bent, hinge forward at the hips until torso is near parallel to floor
• Keep upper arms close to your torso and parallel to the floor
• Extend your forearms straight back until arms are fully extended
• Squeeze your triceps at the top
• Bend elbows to return with control

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.description: Stand at a cable station with a bar or rope attachment at head height. Press the weight straight down until your arms are fully extended. Keep elbows pinned at your sides throughout.

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.description: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms locked. Lower your body by bending the elbows until upper arms are parallel to the floor, keeping your torso upright and elbows close to your body, then press back up. Emphasises the triceps over the chest.

exercises.name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
exercises.description:
• Sit at a lat pulldown station, thighs secured under the pads
• Grip a wide bar with an underhand (supinated) grip
• Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and back
• Squeeze your lats at the bottom
• Let the bar rise with control back to full arm extension

exercises.name: Upright Cable Row
exercises.description:
• Attach a straight bar to a low pulley
• Grip the bar with hands slightly less than shoulder width, pronated grip, bar resting on your thighs
• Pull the bar straight up toward your chin, leading with your elbows
• Elbows rise above your wrists
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Upright Row (DB)
exercises.description:
• Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, pronated grip slightly narrower than shoulder width
• Keep your back straight
• Pull the dumbbells straight up toward your chin, leading with your elbows
• Elbows rise above your wrists
• Lower with control

exercises.name: V-Bar Pulldown
exercises.description: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a V-Bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.

exercises.name: V-Bar Pullup
exercises.description:
• Attach a V-bar to a pull-up bar, or use a station with neutral-grip handles
• Hang with palms facing each other
• Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar
• Squeeze your lats at the top
• Lower with control back to a full hang

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.description: Step forward into a lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor. Drive off the front foot and step forward with the rear foot into the next lunge. Keep torso upright throughout.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description:
• Lie on a flat bench, feet flat on the floor
• Grip the bar with a wide, pronated grip, about 3 inches wider than shoulder width per hand
• Unrack and lower the bar to your chest
• Press back up to full extension
• Keep wrists stacked over elbows throughout

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Bent-Over Row (BB)
exercises.description:
• Hold a barbell with a wide, overhand grip
• Hinge forward at the hips, knees slightly bent, torso near parallel to floor
• Let the bar hang at arm's length
• Row the bar to your lower chest, driving elbows out and back
• Lower with control

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pulldown Behind The Neck
exercises.description:
• Sit at a lat pulldown station, thighs secured under the pads
• Grip a wide bar with a pronated (palms-forward) grip
• Pull the bar down behind your head to your upper traps
• Squeeze your lats at the bottom
• Let the bar rise with control back to full arm extension

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Rear Pull-Up
exercises.description:
• Grip a pull-up bar with a wide, pronated grip
• Lean your torso and head forward so an imaginary line runs from the bar to the back of your neck
• Pull yourself up until the bar reaches behind your neck/upper traps
• Squeeze your back at the top
• Lower with control back to a full hang

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Upright Row (BB)
exercises.description: Hold a barbell with a wide overhand grip. Pull straight up to chin height leading with elbows flaring out to the sides to emphasise rear delts and traps. Lower with control.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl (DB/BB)
exercises.description: Sit with forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, palms up, holding a barbell or dumbbells. Curl the wrists upward as far as possible, then lower slowly. Isolates the forearm flexors.

exercises.name: Wrist Rotations with Straight Bar
exercises.description:
• Hold a barbell with both hands, palms facing down, shoulder-width apart
• Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width
• Alternately roll your wrists, extending one hand up and the other down, as if rolling up a newspaper
• Keep your forearms still — movement stays at the wrist
• Continue alternating for the set

exercises.name: Zottman Curl
exercises.description: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso. Make sure the palms of the hands are facing each other. This will be your starting position.
